acquisitions.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Welcome DuckLabs to the team, Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), and more (August 31, 2026)
acquisitions.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has signed a definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs, an Amsterdam-based company behind the open-source analytical database DuckDB. Co-founded by Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt, DuckLabs created DuckDB to run in-process and execute SQL directly against file formats including Parquet, CSV, and JSON. The database runs locally or on Amazon S3, making it particularly fast for everyday queries of a terabyte or less that form the bulk of real-world analytics. DuckDB also integrates effectively with artificial intelligence agents that explore data similarly to human users. Under the terms of the agreement, DuckDB will remain open source under its independent foundation and the MIT licence. Co-founders Mühleisen and Raasveldt will maintain their roles leading the technical direction of the database. Over time, Amazon Web Services plans to combine the query speed of DuckDB with its existing enterprise-scale analytics offerings. These services include Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon SageMaker. Further technical insights regarding the acquisition and changing analytics practices were shared by Andy Warfield, Vice President and Distinguished Engineer at Amazon Web Services, on the All Things Distributed platform.

launches.title: Kimi K3 by Moonshot AI is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
launches.excerpt: Amazon Bedrock has expanded its open weight model portfolio by making Kimi K3 from Moonshot AI generally available on the platform. The new model is designed to support coding and knowledge work for users requiring high performance. Moonshot AI states that Kimi K3 is its most capable model and marks the first open model to achieve 2.8 trillion parameters. It features native vision capabilities along with a 1-million-token context window. These capabilities render it suitable for long-running coding sessions across extensive repositories, multi-document analysis involving scanned pages and screenshots, and extended agent workflows. Furthermore, Moonshot AI reports that the model achieves an approximate 2.5 times improvement in scaling efficiency compared to Kimi K2. Within Amazon Bedrock, Kimi K3 operates under the same security boundary as proprietary models, utilizing identical controls for access, encryption, and auditing. It is also the first open weight model on Amazon Bedrock to support explicit prompt caching, which helps to decrease latency and input costs when context is reused across model calls. Kimi K3 can be accessed across all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock operates through cross-Region inferencing. Customers can begin using the model by accessing the Amazon Bedrock Console or reviewing the associated documentation.

launches.title: The new AgentCore Runtime is now available in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced the availability of the next generation of AgentCore Runtime, which operates as the serverless microVM compute within Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The updated system introduces elastic memory management designed to reclaim unused memory throughout a session. This approach allows users to pay for their actual resource usage rather than peak capacity. Additionally, the new runtime provides consistent cold start times regardless of concurrency or container image size. The service retains its original serverless features, including scale-to-zero capabilities, hardware-enforced session isolation, and no requirement for pre-provisioning. launches.title: AWS PrivateLink announces Tunnel Endpoints to access network segments
launches.excerpt: AWS PrivateLink customers can now utilise VPC endpoints to access network segments in another VPC or account privately and securely. A new type of VPC endpoint, known as a tunnel endpoint, allows users to tunnel into a specific network segment to reach resources located within it. AWS PrivateLink provides highly available and scalable private access across VPC and account boundaries to load balanced services, appliances, databases, and domains. Prior to this release, sharing resources with external parties required creating an individual Resource Configuration for every single resource. Customers can now generate a Resource Configuration that represents a CIDR range within their network and share it via AWS Resource Access Manager. External vendors can subsequently set up a tunnel endpoint and use GENEVE encapsulation to access the specified CIDR range. Usage incurs an hourly fee for the tunnel endpoint alongside a charge for each gigabyte of data processed through it. The new capability has been launched across numerous global locations, including regions in North America, South America, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, and Mexico. Detailed instructions and setup guidance have been published within the official AWS PrivateLink documentation.

launches.title: New low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances are generally available
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances. Powered by custom sixth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors, these instances are available exclusively on the AWS platform. They are designed to deliver up to 30% better price performance compared to previous-generation T3 instances. The T8i instance family caters to low-to-moderate CPU utilisation workloads, including microservices, staging environments, low-traffic websites, and small databases. Four specific instance sizes are offered, each featuring two vCPUs configured as a single core with unique vCPU-to-memory ratios. Operating on a CPU credit system, T8i instances launch with Unlimited credit mode set as the default configuration. For larger workload requirements, AWS recommends M8i Flex instances, which scale up to 16xlarge. The new instances are currently accessible across multiple global AWS Regions, including locations in North America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific region. Customers can acquire T8i instances through On-Demand and Spot options, with Savings Plan support expected in the near future. Additionally, the t8i.micro and t8i.small sizes have been made available under the AWS Free Tier, although the overall T8i family supports shared tenancy exclusively.
